newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FOCUS-Expansion plans go Latin for Hoyts.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Expansion plans go Latin for Hoyts.

text.p: Australian cinema group Hoyts Cinemas Ltd on Wednesday increased the tempo of its expansion into Latin America with a move into the region's biggest market Brazil and neighbouring Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay.
Hoyts will fund the entry into the Latin markets through a A$95 million one-for-six rights issue also announced today.
The expansion follows hot on the heels of Hoyts' recent moves into Chile and Mexico, where it bought a 35 percent stake in cinema chain Cinemax last November.

Hoyts said it had formed a joint venture with South American property group Raghsa Construcciones S.A. to develop about 300 cinema screens in Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay and Paraguay. Most of the screens will be in Argentina and Brazil, it said.
It said it had also secured four sites with 42 screens in northern Argentina including a 'flagship' megaplex - a complex with more than 16 screens - in Buenos Aires.

"It is widely acknowledged that the Latin American markets are currently underscreened, providing substantial opportunity for multiplex development," Hoyts chief executive officer Peter Ivany said in a statement.
"Argentina also represents one of these underdeveloped markets, with the potential for significant growth," Ivany said.
"I would think over the next few years we will have over 600 screens throughout Latin America," Ivany told reporters in a conference call from London.

Hoyts plans to become a major world cinema operator with plans to operate 2,800 screens worldwide by 2001, compared with about 1,220 at the moment. It has about 820 screens in the United States, where it is the 10th largest cinema group.

The rest of Hoyts cinemas are in Australia, New Zealand, Chile and Mexico. Hoyts' ambitious target is almost on a par with Australian rival, Village Roadshow Ltd, which plans to operate 3,000 screens worldwide by 2000.
The Sydney-based Hoyts plans to announce its expansion into Britain shortly, where Ivany is currently.

Ivany said Hoyts has secured a site at the Bluewater retail complex in Kent, southern England. Australian media have reported Hoyts would construct a 20 screen complex at Bluewater. In Europe, Hoyts is also targetting Germany and Austria and plans to operate 300 screens across Europe by 2000.

Hoyts' rights issue, which was priced at A$2.40 per share compared with the close of A$2.70 on Wednesday, was its second capital raising since its A$100 million float last August. In November it raised A$61.1 million through a placement.
Ivany said following the issue Hoyts will have A$200 million to fund its expansion plans and capital expenditure.
The increase in share capital will dilute the stake held by its major shareholder, U.S. investment bank Hellman & Friedman, to 36.7 percent from 42.9 percent previously.
Its other major shareholder, Australian property and investment group Lend Lease Corp Ltd, will have its shareholding diluted to 7.5 percent from 8.8 percent.
The issue would not affect earnings forecasts, Hoyts said.
It said it expected earnings would not be less than the 1996 prospectus forecasts of A$22 million net profit for the year to June 30, 1997.
